title: Record the B1 operator decision safely — prepared, previewed, deliberately not recorded

1_recorded_or_templated.and_the_reason_is_measured_not_cautious: The stage offers Option 1 when unsure the code can hold a partial B1 decision safely. It can — proved by simulation below, orders_possible stays false in every shape. The refusal is on the MERITS: neither decision is TRUE today.

2_which_decision_type.legacy_retired_confirmed: says legacy has stopped trading. MEASURED: legacy is DORMANT, not retired. track1-only-shadow registers 0 legacy strategy jobs; the default mode registers 45. The difference is ONE command-line flag, so this claim is falsified by a plain restart while the gate goes on reading it as true. Retiring legacy is the ordered procedure in the switch-over runbook section 3, which has not been executed — and its 11 drain jobs are still scheduled, which this stage was told not to disable.
2_which_decision_type.separate_account_confirmed: says Track 1 has its own IBKR login. There is one account (equity 996,883) and nothing in this system has ever observed a second one.
2_which_decision_type.whose_call: the operator's. The runbook says the confirmation file is written by a person, never by a script — and that includes this one.

3_which_measurement_record.note: the 24h expiry is deliberate: an account flat yesterday is not evidence about the account now, so the gate closes again on its own

4_b1_released_or_pending.why: the measured half passes; the decided half is empty

5_other_blockers.proved_structurally: both are MEASURED_GATEs with released_by == (), and self_check refuses a MEASURED_GATE that any confirmation flag could open. No decision file can reach them.

9_legacy_drain_safety.and_a_decision_cannot_change_that: the scheduler is built from command-line flags and never reads the confirmation file — asserted by AST, so recording a decision cannot remove the drain

what_was_built.global_index/track1_b1_decision.py: a read-only previewer: given a candidate decision file it reports what would open, what would stay shut, whether orders would become possible, the live measurement and when it expires, and whether the RUNNING scheduler can still open a legacy position. It has no code path that writes anything — asserted behaviourally by watching every file opened for writing, and again by AST, and it never names the live confirmation path.
what_was_built.scratch/track1_b1_decision_template_2026: inert by construction. A verbatim copy to the live path is refused for TWO independent reasons — unknown underscore keys, and an empty confirmed_by — and a test proves the plural by ablation: each defence is removed in turn and refusal must survive.
what_was_built.global_index/track1_paper_readiness.py: its closing paragraph said B1 was released by 'a confirmation file'. True until 5ZQ and quietly wrong afterwards. It now reports B1 as TWO halves — decision pending/recorded, measurement PASS/stale/missing — and states that no gate builds an order path.

the_finding_that_settled_option_1.so: legacy's dormancy is a runtime flag, not a retirement. Recording legacy_retired_confirmed today would freeze a claim that `ops.py restart --scheduler` (without the flag) silently falsifies.
the_finding_that_settled_option_1.what_was_done_about_it: the previewer says this at the moment of decision — the only moment it helps — rather than folding it into PASS/FAIL, because for a SEPARATE ACCOUNT decision legacy entry jobs running is correct, not a fault

regression.what_the_sweep_uncovered: three failures in the LEDGER suites, which the 5ZQ bisect had not covered because those suites were not among the 14 it ran. One of the three is mine.

gate_and_readiness_sweep_AFTER_the_fixes.all_five_were_ledger_parity: three fixed by regenerating the record and the document, one by teaching the satisfiability test the second kind of measurement, and two more that were reading the same record

the_one_this_stage_caused_and_the_test_w.what_it_asserts: the whole blocker set must be SATISFIABLE, and not by signatures alone: hold each measurement shut in turn and exactly the gates depending on it must be the ones still refusing
the_one_this_stage_caused_and_the_test_w.why_it_fired: Stage 5ZQ introduced a SECOND KIND of measurement. `released_by_measurement` is an OR — passing OPENS the gate. The new `also_requires_measurement` is an AND — passing is REQUIRED even once the gate is signed. The loop only knew the first kind, so `legacy_broker_flat` came back as 'releases no order-blocking gate'. The test was correct on its own terms.
the_one_this_stage_caused_and_the_test_w.fix: both kinds are covered now, with the same claim for each: hold the measurement shut and exactly the gates that depend on it must refuse. For an AND-measurement that is the STRONGER statement, because the gate refuses with every signature already granted.
the_one_this_stage_caused_and_the_test_w.and_it_got_stronger: a new assertion was added while I was in there — granting ONLY the waiver flags, with every measurement held shut, must open nothing. The escape hatch built for 'the broker could not be reached' must never become a way in.
